In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the simplex system is more reliable than the selective redundant systems for a constant failure rate and the selective redundant systems are more reliable for a time dependent failure rate.
for a given reliability requirement, a redundant system may not be the best alternative.

for a given reliability requirement, the redundant configuration may be more economical than the simplex configuration, provided that the failure time distribution of the units and the mission time are known and the cost of redundancy can be justified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a given mission time, the reliability of a redundant system may be lower than that of the simplex system, and vice versa.

the reliability of a redundant system is not necessarily better than the reliability of a simplex system, and the choice of system configuration should not be based on the reliability of the system alone, but on the cost, complexity and the failure rate of the units.
the simplex system may have the best performance when the system is required to operate for a long duration of time and the failure time of units are constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the system reliability is not always proportional to its mean-time-to-fail.
the reliability analysis of a system should be based on a comprehensive study of the reliability network, the unit failure rate, the system mission time and the failure time distribution.
the system configuration is a critical factor in determining the system mean-time-between-failures.
